{{Quote|An intelligent and peaceful man, he has always been, and hard to believe, it is, that he would endanger the Sephi without cause.|[[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]]|<ref name="JediYoda" />}}
'''Alaric''' was a [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Sephi/Legends|Sephi]] and the [[King/Legends|king]] of [[Thustra/Legends|Thustra]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. He was a friend of [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Grand Master/Legends|Grand Master]] [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]] for some 200 [[Standard year/Legends|years]], despite their friendship being somewhat strained by the demanding nature of their positions. When the war between the Republic and the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatists]] erupted, Alaric chose to leave the Republic, seeing corruption in the government and believed that joining with the Separatist Alliance would restore order.

When the Republic [[Battle of Thustra|sent a force]] to Thustra, Alaric's friend, Grand Master Yoda, wanted to negotiate with the monarch for a peaceful solution. In the ensuing talks, Alaric tried to convince Yoda to join him on his side, since he stated that he was on the wrong side of the war. However, Alaric's nephew [[Navi]] manipulated both the Republic and the Jedi, resulting in a battle. Alaric forced his old friend to kill him in self-defense. The death of the king caused the neighboring worlds to send their armies to Thustra, so that the Republic had to retire.

==Biography==
[[File:AlaricDeath.jpg|thumb|left|100px|The death of King Alaric]]
200 years before the outbreak of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], King Alaric ruled over the Sephi and the planet Thustra as king. At some point, had encountered the Jedi Grand Master Yoda, thus leading to a friendship that would last all the way to the start of the galaxy-wide conflict though it would lessened over time due to their respective leadership roles. By the time of the Clone Wars, King Alaric grew disgusted by [[Navi|his nephew's]] behavior in the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Senate]] and the corruption in the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. Although he and his people had kept their silence hoping that the Republic would come to see the error of its ways, it had been misconstrued as support for the Republic. Alaric eventually had enough, especially after the Republic's attempts to force the Sephi's allegiance. He thus contacted [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] and offered to join the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]]. 

When Thustra announced its intention to leave the Republic, [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] ordered Generals [[Tyffix]] and [[Tyr]] to lead the Republic's forces on the planet, hoping that such a display of power would force the Sephi to change their minds. Instead, the Sephi attacked with suicide bombers and decimated their forces. Tyffix and Tyr were killed, leaving their inexperienced padawans, [[Cal (Jedi)|Cal]] and [[Pix (Jedi)|Pix]] to lead the clone forces. 

Knowing that the secession of Thustra would lead the [[Sumitra sector/Legends|Sumitra sector]] to join ranks with the Seperatists, Chancellor Palpatine sent Yoda to negotiate with King Alaric as their friendship would be key to bringing about a peaceful resolution. Yoda landed on Thustra and brought the reluctant Cal along with him to meet with King Alaric in his [[Alaric's palace|throne room]]. Although the reception Yoda and Cal received was initially warm due to Yoda and Alaric's friendship, it changed when Yoda brought up the issue of Thustra's withdrawal from the Republic. Alaric stated his reasons for having Thustra secede, saddening Yoda who had hoped to convince Alaric to change his mind. Alaric refused, as the Sephi's hearts and minds were with the king and were ready to die for Thustra. 

It was then that Navi burst into the throne room and angrily criticized his uncle for making what he believed to be a disastrous decision. Alaric rebuked Navi for questioning his reasoning when he knew full well that Navi was only interested in staying with the Republic to profit from the corruption itself. Alaric once more stated that there was nothing to discuss, leading Yoda to implore his old friend to rethink this decision. Instead, Alaric ordered his guards to take Yoda and Cal prisoner in order to prevent them from returning with a clone army. Despite this, Alaric already had many regrets and that there might be more before the end.

Sometime later, Alaric summoned Yoda to his [[Alaric's garden|royal garden]] where they could talk more openly without fear of the court listening in on their discussion. Yoda and Alaric  expressed their sadness at not having stayed in touch over the years before the king led the Jedi Master on a tour of his garden. Among the garden was a [[Century flower|rare vegetal species]] from the far side of the galaxy that Alaric had nurtured and tended to for a century. The king compared his garden and the fragile ecosystem to the galaxy made up of planets and systems, as a metaphor to explain why Thustra needed to leave the Republic. Alaric explained that he was not disloyal to the Republic and intended to rejoin when the corruption was gone.<ref name="JediYoda" /> He then commended Yoda for having such honorable and true motives in serving the Republic, but then implored him to realize that the Jedi was on the wrong side of the conflict. Yoda gently disagreed and stated that although the Republic had been stained by political bickering and greed, he still had an obligation to uphold its founding principles. Despite being saddened that Yoda and Alaric failed once more to come to an agreeable outcome, Alaric decided to release Yoda and Cal. To that end, he returned their lightsabers and cautioned them against his nephew Navi who would no doubt conspire against the Jedi.

True enough, Navi and [[Moje]] had been busy with their machinations. Moje tricked Cal into trying to escape to the Republic while Navi lied to the Republic's forces by saying that his uncle had ordered Yoda's and Cal's executions. Navi tricked the Jedi and clone troopers into a preemptive strike against the Sephi forces and against the palace grounds. Their plot succeeded to such devastating results as Cal had fallen for Moje's lies and found himself against several palace guards whom Moje had deceived into thinking the Jedi planned to assassinate the king. Yoda and Cal fought back against the guards only for Cal to be shot and killed, while Pix's forces decimated the Sephi forces and rained down destruction upon the Sephi capital.

King Alaric watched in mourning as the battle spilled over into his palace and his garden became an unfortunate victim of collateral damage. Yoda arrived at the garden where the king held his special flower in a glass case and implored Alaric to stand down his forces and surrender. The monarch refused as his people needed a means to fight on no matter the cost. In order to galvanize his people to fight on no matter the cost, he drew a blaster from his robes and aimed it at Yoda, who was forced to deflect the [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] bolt back into Alaric's body. As the monarch lay dying, he gifted Yoda with his prized flower and pleaded for Yoda to cherish their friendship from earlier times. With his last words, King Alaric died a martyr for his people.

== Legacy ==
After King Alaric's death, Navi returned to the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] on Coruscant to spread false news about the deaths of Master Yoda and to ensure that Thustra would remain in the Republic. However, Yoda arrived with [[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]] and a contingent of clone troopers, who placed the corrupt senator under arrest for crimes against the Republic and conspiracy to commit murder. As a resistant Navi was being led away screaming that he served his people, Chancellor Palpatine welcomed back Yoda and expressed relief that Yoda had survived. Yoda took no comfort in this due to the death of his friend Alaric whom he had been forced to kill in order to defend himself. 

Alaric's death did indeed unite the Sephi and the other systems in Thustra's sector against the Republic. Those same systems sent aid to the Sephi and Count Dooku's droid armies were sent to bolster their strength. With Thustra being completely lost to the Republic, the Clone Wars would escalate and force the Jedi to send more of their number to fight.

Yoda returned to his [[Yoda's quarters|quarters]] at the Jedi Temple and kept Alaric's prized flowers as a reminder of the friendship he once shared with King Alaric. He would also begin to harbor doubts that the war was worth all the death and destruction that had been wrought.

== Personality and traits ==
{{Quote|Alaric is anything but a disgruntled monarch. His people love him, and his influence extends beyond his own planet.|Supreme Chancellor Palpatine|<ref name="JediYoda" />}}
King Alaric had been described by Master Yoda as an intelligent and peaceful who truly held his people's best interests at heart unlike his nephew Navi who was as self-serving as the majority of the Republic Senate. As a wise and highly influential leader who was beloved by his own people, the Sephi looked to Alaric for guidance and leadership in all matters as did many systems within Thustra's sector.

As king, Alaric had become disillusioned by the corruption running rampant in the Galactic Republic and the fact that his own nephew had been taken in by the moral decay. Because of this, the king would find himself completely at odds with Navi, who was adamantly opposed to following his uncle's lead and giving up his own interests for the Sephi's sake.

Although Alaric was normally a reasonable man, he was also a man of strong principles and deep conviction in that he believed that leaving the Republic was the best course of action for Thustra and the Sephi. As such, there was nothing that Yoda could say or do that would convince Alaric to change his mind and vice versa. Despite this, the monarch was not disloyal to the Republic. He believed that the Clone Wars would end one day and that the Republic would get its affairs in order. On that day, Alaric swore to Yoda that Thustra would return to the fold.

Just as his people were ready to die for their king, so too was Alaric ready to die for the Sephi. In fact, this was proven true when the machinations of his nephew brought the Republic and the king's forces into open battle. At that moment, Alaric showed no regard for self-preservation as he drew a blaster and fired on Yoda, thus forcing the diminutive Jedi to kill his old friend.

In his spare time, Alaric was known to be an avid gardener and kept a greenhouse where he would tend to his flowers with great care. He would see his garden as an analogy for the galaxy and its governments; such a garden needed great patience and attention to ensure that each flower needed space of its own and to keep hostile species in check in order to ensure harmony.
